items.title: The Fifth Limb, and What Makes This Concentration "Noble"

items.zh: 又於第五喻有差別。於所觀相慇懃懇到等，當知已如前釋。謂審觀察三世諸行，於能觀察又復觀察，是此中總義。
items.en: Again, for the fifth there is a difference in the simile. "Earnestly and thoroughly taking up the mark contemplated," and so on, should be known as already explained [in fascicle 11]. Its general sense here is: closely contemplating the formations of the three times, and, upon the very act of contemplating, contemplating again.

items.zh: 何等名為聖三摩地？云何建立五支差別？謂四靜慮中，所有聖賢心一境性，及於安立審諦觀察，如是名為聖三摩地。依於四種現法樂住，建立四支；依審觀察緣起法故，又為斷除餘結縛故，建立第五。當知此由二因緣故，建立五支。
items.en: What is a noble concentration? How are the five limbs established? In the four dhyānas, the noble ones' one-pointedness of mind, and their close, careful contemplation of what is established — this is a noble concentration. On the four pleasant abidings in this very life, the four limbs are established; on the close contemplation of dependent origination, and further, on the severing of the remaining fetters and bonds, the fifth is established. Know that by these two conditions the fifth limb is established.

items.title: The Noble Right Concentration, With Cause and Equipment: Five Factors That Lead In

items.zh: 復次，云何有因有具聖正三摩地？當知善故，及無漏故，說名為聖。有五道支名此定因。所謂正見、正思惟、正語、正業、正命。具有三種。所謂正見、正精進、正念。此中薄伽梵總說前七道支，與聖正三摩地為因為具。隨其所應，差別當知。謂由前導次第義故，立五為因；於三摩地資助義故，立三為具。
items.en: Furthermore, what is the noble right concentration with cause and with equipment? Know that because it is wholesome and because it is uncontaminated, it is called noble. Five path-factors are named the cause of this concentration: right view, right thought, right speech, right action, and right livelihood. Its equipment is threefold: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness. Here the Blessed One broadly declared the prior seven path-factors to be the cause and the equipment of the noble right concentration; their difference should be known accordingly — because of the sense of leading-in-sequence, five are set up as the cause; because of the sense of assisting the concentration, three are set up as the equipment.

items.zh: 云何正見等前導次第義？謂先了知世間實有真阿羅漢正行正至，便於出離深生樂欲，獲得正見。次復思惟：何當出離居家迫迮，乃至廣說。從此出家，受學尸羅，修治淨命。是名正語、正業、正命。
items.en: What is the sense in which right view and the rest lead in sequence? First one comes to know that in the world there truly are real arhats of right conduct and right attainment, and so generates a deep desire for release, gaining right view. Next one reflects: "I should leave the cramp of household life," and so on at length. Thereupon one goes forth, takes up the training of the precepts, and purifies one's livelihood — this is right speech, right action, and right livelihood.

items.title: The Equipment That Assists It: Right View, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness

items.zh: 此正見等，於所對治邪見等五猶未能斷。還即依止此五善法，從他聞音，展轉發生聞慧正見。為欲斷除所治法故，又為修習道資糧故，方便觀察。次依聞慧發生思慧，復依思慧發生修慧。
items.en: This right view and the rest cannot yet sever the five to be countered — wrong view and the rest. Still relying on these five wholesome factors, and hearing the teaching from another, one progressively gives rise to the right view of hearing-wisdom. In order to sever what is to be countered, and to cultivate the provisions for the path, one skilfully investigates: then, upon hearing-wisdom, reflection-wisdom arises, and upon reflection-wisdom, cultivation-wisdom.

items.zh: 由此正見，於諸邪見，如實了知此是邪見；於諸正見，如實了知此是正見；乃至正命，如實知已。為欲斷除邪見等故，及為圓滿正見等故，發勤精進。若由此故，能斷所治，集能治法，令其圓滿，是名正念。此念即是三摩地分，故亦兼說正三摩地。
items.en: By this right view, one knows wrong views as they are — "this is wrong view" — and right views as they are — "this is right view" — up through right livelihood, known as it is. In order to sever wrong view and the rest, and to fulfil right view and the rest, one rouses diligent effort. If by this one can sever what is to be countered and gather the countering factors to fullness, this is right mindfulness. This mindfulness is itself a concentration-factor, so right concentration too is implied along with it.

items.title: When Right Concentration Is Fulfilled, and the Three Trainings Complete Together

items.zh: 若是時中，捨邪見等令不復生，修正見等令得圓滿；即於如是方便道中，亦能棄捨邪精進念，兼能修滿正精進念。若於是時，於彼諸法能斷能滿；即於此時，聖正三摩地亦得圓滿。
items.en: When, at that time, one abandons wrong view and the rest so they arise no more, and cultivates right view and the rest to fullness — then, on that very preparatory path, one is also able to cast off wrong effort and wrong mindfulness, and to cultivate right effort and right mindfulness to fullness. When, at that time, one can sever and can fulfil those factors, then at that very time the noble right concentration too is fulfilled.

items.zh: 此中由慧為導首，於增上戒先自安處。次聞他音、如理作意，及增上戒學二為依止，於方便道中，發生增上心學及增上慧學。此中正念，名增上心學；正見、正精進，名增上慧學。如是三學，於修聖正三摩地時，皆得圓滿。
items.en: Herein, with wisdom as the leader, one first settles oneself in the higher training in precepts. Next, with hearing the teaching, sound attention, and the higher training in precepts together as its basis, on the preparatory path one gives rise to the higher training in mind and the higher training in wisdom. Here right mindfulness is called the higher training in mind; right view and right effort are called the higher training in wisdom. These three trainings are all fulfilled at the time of cultivating the noble right concentration.

items.title: The Vajra-Like Concentration: The Blow That Ends the Trainee's Path

items.zh: 復次，云何金剛喻三摩地？謂最後邊學三摩地。此三摩地最第一故，最尊勝故，極堅牢故，上無煩惱能摧伏故，摧伏一切諸煩惱故，是故此定名金剛喻。譬如金剛，其性堅固，諸末尼等不能穿壞，穿壞一切末尼寶等。此定亦爾，故喻金剛。
items.en: Furthermore, what is the vajra-like concentration? The concentration at the very last stage of a trainee. Because this concentration is the foremost, the most excellent, and the utterly firm; because no affliction above it can crush it, and it crushes all afflictions — for these reasons this concentration is called "vajra-like." Just as vajra, firm by nature, cannot be pierced or broken by any maṇi-jewel and the rest, yet pierces and breaks all maṇi-jewels — this concentration too is such, and so is likened to vajra.

items.title: The Five Direct-Seeing Attainments: Impurity, Consciousness's Flow, and Severance

items.zh: 復次，云何五現見三摩鉢底？謂諸苾芻，即於此身等，廣說如經。已見諦者修此等至，是故名為現見等至。是諸修道所斷煩惱制伏對治、斷滅對治，及觀察斷。當知此中總略體性。初不淨觀，方便念住以為依止，為令欲貪不現行故，觀察內身種種不淨。第二不淨觀，即彼念住以為依止，乃至觀察骨人之相，為令彼貪不現行故，觀察此身種種不淨。當知齊此，名具觀察一切不淨。最極通達者，是青瘀等觀品類次第、極逾越義。初不淨觀，觀察內身現前安住種種不淨。後不淨觀，通達法性。觀察此身有如是法，有如是性，乃至廣說。
items.en: Furthermore, what are the five direct-seeing attainments? Monks who, within this very body, [contemplate], as the scripture explains at length. One who has already seen the truths cultivates these attainments, so they are called direct-seeing attainments. Their general nature here is the countering-by-subduing, the countering-by-severing, and the contemplation-of-severance of the afflictions abandoned on the path of cultivation. The first impurity contemplation, resting on the preparatory foundation of mindfulness, contemplates the manifold impurities of the internal body, so that craving-desire may not manifest. The second, resting on that same foundation, contemplates on up to the mark of the skeleton, so that that craving may not manifest — know that this far is called the complete contemplation of all impurity. The later impurity contemplation penetrates the dharma-nature: contemplating that this body has such a nature, such a character, and so on at length.

items.zh: 觀識流轉者，觀察此識生滅相續。或觀生身展轉相續。謂麁觀察行緣識等。或觀剎那展轉相續。謂細觀察若有貪心、離貪心等品類差別，荏苒過度彼彼日夜、剎那、臘縛、牟呼栗多，於其中間非一眾多種種心識異生異滅。觀察有學未離欲者，俱住二世；已離欲者，惟住他世；阿羅漢果，俱無所住。如是名為觀察於斷。
items.en: Contemplating the flow of consciousness: contemplating this consciousness's arising-and-perishing continuity — either contemplating the successive continuity of the reborn body (the coarse contemplation of formations conditioning consciousness and the rest), or contemplating momentary succession (the fine contemplation of the varied kinds of mind — with craving, freed of craving, and so on — as, through the passing days and nights, moments and hours, not one but many manifold mind-consciousnesses arise diversely and perish diversely). Contemplating severance: a trainee not yet free of desire dwells in both worlds; one already free of desire dwells only in the other world; at the fruit of arhatship, one dwells in neither. This is called the contemplation of severance.

blocks.text: Today's reading places concentration within the eightfold path. "Noble right concentration" has causes and equipment drawn from the other path factors; when it is fulfilled, the three trainings are complete together. At the end of the path stands the **vajra-like concentration**, the final blow that ends the trainee's path.

The fifth limb is the **reviewing mark** (觀察相): seeing the concentration from outside, as one standing sees one sitting, or one sitting sees one lying. This concentration is "noble" because it is "the one-pointedness of the worthy and noble" in the four dhyānas. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "worthy" (who practise the foundations of mindfulness before seeing the truths) also have this one-pointedness, as do the noble.

**Noble right concentration** has a cause and equipment. "Five path-factors are named its cause: right view, right thought, right speech, right action, and right livelihood." Its equipment: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness. Concentration on the path does not stand alone; it grows out of ethics and is supported by view, effort, and mindfulness.

The sequence begins with faith: one learns that there truly are arhats, and gains right view. Venerable Miào Jìng: "He believes there truly are noble ones and that ordinary beings can become noble." Then, "May I too leave home!" (Venerable Miào Jìng reads 何 as "may": "I too can go forth"). Then hearing, reflection, and cultivation. He adds: hearing-wisdom "has no power to subdue afflictions"; reflection-wisdom does. Study alone is not enough; one must think it through.

When right concentration is fulfilled, the three trainings are complete together: right mindfulness and concentration are the training in mind; right view and effort, the training in wisdom; right speech, action, and livelihood, the training in discipline. Master Cháng Bǎi notes that the assignment names only the most prominent factors; right thought belongs to wisdom too.

"The concentration at the very last stage of a trainee" is called **vajra-like** (金剛喻定): "just as vajra, firm by nature, cannot be pierced or broken by any jewel, yet pierces all", this concentration cannot be broken by any affliction and breaks the last. Venerable Miào Jìng: it is the most excellent "among persons", among all trainee noble ones; immediately after it, one becomes an arhat.

Those who have seen the truths cultivate five "attainments of direct seeing": contemplating impurity; the flow of consciousness; severance; and others. Master Cháng Bǎi converts the units of the flow of consciousness: 120 moments make a *tatkṣaṇa*, 60 of those a *lava*, 30 *lavas* a *muhūrta*. Seeing consciousness at this resolution is seeing its impermanence directly.

On severance, Venerable Miào Jìng reads 住 as "attachment": one free of desire no longer clings to this world, though still to the next. Severance proceeds world by world, as it did realm by realm on Day 74.

quiz.q: The noble concentration is "the one-pointedness of the noble and worthy" in the four dhyānas. The note limits it to stream-enterers and above. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: worthy and noble are distinct — the worthy (practising mindfulness before seeing the truths) also have one-pointedness, as do the noble
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "At the worthy stage there's one-pointedness, and at the noble stage still one-pointedness." Master Cháng Bǎi: "noble" may be those past seeing, "worthy" those in the preparatory stage. The note and translation's "noble ones" alone narrow it (logged).

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which path factors are the "cause" and the "equipment" of noble right concentration?
options: cause: right view, thought, speech, action, livelihood; equipment: right view, effort, mindfulness
quiz.why: "Five path-factors are named the cause of this concentration: right view, right thought, right speech, right action, and right livelihood. Its equipment is threefold: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the five are distant causes, the three proximate conditions.

quiz.q: The sequence begins by knowing there truly are arhats, then gaining right view. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this right view is?
options: faith that there are noble ones and that ordinary people can become noble — right view here is faith plus aspiration
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "He believes there truly are noble ones and that ordinary beings can become noble — he has faith in this." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pixunji*: ordinary beings too can practise the first seven path factors.

quiz.q: Hearing-wisdom gives rise to reflection-wisdom, then cultivation-wisdom. How much power over afflictions does each have, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: hearing-wisdom has no power to subdue afflictions; reflection-wisdom does
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Hearing-wisdom has no power — none at all to subdue afflictions; reflection-wisdom has power." His example: the person before me isn't the one who insulted me; resenting him reveals a view of permanence. Master Cháng Bǎi: hear, then reflect, then hear again.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the vajra-like concentration, and why "vajra"?
options: the trainee's very last concentration — like vajra, unpierced by any jewel yet piercing all
quiz.why: "The concentration at the very last stage of a trainee … Just as vajra, firm by nature, cannot be pierced or broken by any maṇi-jewel and the rest, yet pierces and breaks all maṇi-jewels." Master Cháng Bǎi: the concentration on which the non-returner or arhat-candidate finally cuts afflictions.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, who cultivates the five direct-seeing attainments, and what is their nature?
options: those who have seen the truths — countering by subduing, countering by severing, and contemplating the severance of afflictions abandoned on the path of cultivation
quiz.why: "One who has already seen the truths cultivates these attainments … Their general nature here is the countering-by-subduing, the countering-by-severing, and the contemplation-of-severance of the afflictions abandoned on the path of cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: inner and outer impurity, coarse and fine consciousness, and severance — five.

quiz.q: Contemplating consciousness's flow mentions moments, lavas, and muhūrtas. How does Master Cháng Bǎi convert them?
options: 120 moments make a tatkṣaṇa, 60 tatkṣaṇas a lava, 30 lavas a muhūrta
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "120 kṣaṇas make a tatkṣaṇa; 60 tatkṣaṇas a lava; 30 lavas a muhūrta, also called a 'moment' (須臾)." The text: across days and nights, moments and hours, countless consciousnesses arise and perish.
